messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: node-gpu-42 reported pod gpu-serve-7 crash (OOM) and kernel message 'CUDA illegal memory access' observed. auto-scaling triggered.
ops-oncall-1: got it, I'm looking. Seeing a bunch of OOM/kern messages on node-gpu-42.
ops-oncall-1: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-serve` -> several restarts.
alex-runtime: pinging in. Any immediate customer impact? julie-cs, do you see errors from any tenants?
julie-cs: small blip on a few customer endpoints, mostly 503s for embed endpoints. CS has inbound tickets from alpha-inc and beta-ops.
ops-oncall-1: grabbing node logs: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 --no-pager` and dmesg shows kernel oops lines referencing misaligned device address during pagewalk.
ranjit-sre: can you paste the dmesg snippet?
ops-oncall-1: ```
[123456.789] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: Xid (GPU page fault): 78, pid=12345, tid=1, fault: UNALIGNED_ADDRESS
[123456.790] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000010
[123456.790] RIP: 0010:0x7f8c0a1e4abc
[123456.791] Call Trace: ... gpu_page_walk+0x2f
```
samir-eng-runtime: that Xid 78 UNALIGNED_ADDRESS matches the CUDA illegal memory access we've seen in staging with that driver variant.
marta-eng: which driver? Did we roll a driver or kernel recently on that pool?
ops-oncall-1: node shows kernel 5.15.0-104 and nvidia-driver 535.54.03, rolled as part of last week's runtime patcher.
alex-runtime: hmm. last week's canary passed on shorter sequences. This workload has long KV cache chains and cold-start pagewalks may exercise edge-case.
ranjit-sre: immediate mitigations: cordon node-gpu-42, drain non-critical pods, and disable GPUPACK for new allocations on the pool. Can we failover requests to CPU workers temporarily?
alex-runtime: yes — switch route policy for model-x to fallback_cpu_variant in router config. I'll flip the flag and fetch logs for errors.
dev-deploy-bot: Deploy started: route-update v2026-11-03-flag -> fallback_cpu_variant for model-x
ops-oncall-1: cordoned and drained. Some pods restarted on other nodes.
julie-cs: CS update: alpha-inc saw ~2m of 503s, we notified them and opened a support ticket. Beta-ops was rate-limited but recovered.
alex-runtime: enabling additional retry/backoff at LB for 30s to reduce client-visible 503s. Also adding a short-term quota bump for critical tenants.
samir-eng-runtime: capturing crashloop logs and container core dump. Uploading to /mnt/incident/artifacts/2790123456/
ops-oncall-1: core dump analysis (prelim): faulting address misaligned with expected page boundaries; appears in GPU driver pagewalk path.
marta-eng: escalating to kernel/driver owners. @ranjit-sre can you open a ticket with driver vendor and attach dmesg, coredump, driver version + repro steps?
ranjit-sre: opened vendor ticket V-2790123456. Steps and artifacts attached.
alex-runtime: rolling a temporary driver rollback proposal: revert to 535.43.x on this pool and re-run smoke tests. That driver didn't show the Xid behavior in Canary last month.
ops-oncall-1: proposal accepted. Scheduling driver rollback on node-gpu-42 and two replicas in pool. ETA 12m.
statusbot: Incident created: GPU-POOL-FAULT-2790123456. Status: investigating. Impact: partial 503s for embeddings/chat. Affected customers: alpha-inc (partial), beta-ops (partial).
ops-oncall-1: performed rollback to 535.43.21 on node-gpu-42, restarted kubelet. Monitoring.
samir-eng-runtime: after rollback, no further Xid 78 in the logs for 8m. Pods that were restarted show no immediate OOM.
julie-cs: updating customers: alpha-inc acknowledged the mitigation, kept ticket open for root-cause.
alex-runtime: routing remains on fallback_cpu_variant for extra safety for 30m. We'll start a canary to gradually move a small % back to GPU on the rolled-back driver.
dev-deploy-bot: Canary started: 3% traffic to GPU pool with 535.43.21 -> gpu-serve-canary-1
ops-oncall-1: canary healthy for 5m. no exceptions.
ranjit-sre: because this is likely a driver/pagewalk race exposed by our long sequences and KV cache patterns, add action items: 1) revert driver in pool until vendor patch, 2) add kernel/driver regression tests with long KV chain patterns, 3) ensure auto-eviction thresholds tuned to avoid noisy restarts.
marta-eng: logging followups for Optimize team: examine cache alignment behavior and guarded allocations in runtime.
alex-runtime: handing off to second-shift SRE. Key context: node-gpu-42 had Xid 78 UNALIGNED_ADDRESS after recent driver roll; rollback to 535.43.21 removed repro; vendor ticket V-2790123456 opened. Fallback routes in place, canary healthy. Artifacts: /mnt/incident/artifacts/2790123456/
ranjit-sre: Handoff ack. Next oncall: @samir-eng-runtime will own until resolved. Please triage vendor responses and escalate if Xid returns.
samir-eng-runtime: ack, taking over. I'll also coordinate a controlled repro in staging with long sequence KV cache stress.
julie-cs: leaving note for customer followup: offer postmortem and timeline when RCA available. :thumbsup:
statusbot: Incident updated: mitigation applied, status: monitoring. Next update in 30m or on change.
ops-oncall-1: closing thread on primary investigation; keeping incident open. If Xid reappears, reopen with priority. Thanks all for quick action. :heart:
